# Researched fight money (generated by `npm run research -- markdown`)

432 claims checked: 275 verified, 118 single_source, 32 unconfirmed, 7 excluded. Verified = quote confirmed on the live page by code and two independent sites (or one official record) agree within 5%. Excluded = taken out of the comparison by a recorded decision (listed at the end, with the reason and evidence). Amounts in US dollars as published (nominal).

## Decisions

Each took a figure out of the cross-check; nothing was added by hand. A figure still needs two independent sources to be verified.

- **hearsay**, 2026-10-03, claude-research: espn.com siteFeeUsd $100,000,000 (Anthony Joshua vs Andy Ruiz Jr.). ESPN does not report the figure itself: it says the nearly $100 million 'has been widely reported in the British media' and that Hearn did not dispute it, naming no outlet. The $40 million has a named origin (Mike Coppinger, The Athletic) and is repeated by three sites, but those three all trace to him, so this is one reporter against an unattributed rumour, not three sources against one; treat the $40 million as the best-supported figure, not a confirmed one. Evidence: https://www.givemesport.com/1496240-saudi-arabia-paid-333m-to-secure-anthony-joshua-vs-andy-ruiz-jr-rematch/, https://www.boxingnews24.com/2019/08/andy-ruiz-vs-anthony-joshua-2-hearn-signed-40m-site-fee-to-bring-it-to-saudi-arabia/
- **outlier**, 2026-10-03, claude-research: bleacherreport.com totalUsd $10,000,000 (Anthony Joshua vs Andy Ruiz Jr.). Pre-fight report of a revised deal ('about $10 million', Coppinger). ESPN's contract figure and a post-fight summary both say $9 million, so the total is recorded at $9 million; the $10 million guarantee stays in the data as its own single-source figure (Gulf News). The real amount lies between $9 million and $10 million and this decision is the least certain one in the set. Evidence: https://www.espn.com/boxing/story/_/id/27386019/ruiz-balks-fighting-joshua-saudi-arabia, https://furyjoshua.com/news/joshua-vs-ruiz-jr-2-results-scorecards-purses/, https://gulfnews.com/sport/ruiz-agrees-to-saudi-rematch-for-a-few-dollars-more-1.65968849
- **floor**, 2026-10-03, claude-research: substack.com ppvBuys 650,000 (Terence Crawford vs Errol Spence Jr.); substack.com ppvBuys 650,000 (Terence Crawford vs Errol Spence Jr.); outkick.com ppvBuys 650,000 (Terence Crawford vs Errol Spence Jr.). Dan Rafael's first report says 'at least 650,000' (OutKick repeats it as 'around 650,000', crediting him, so it is the same report, not a second source). A floor is compatible with the roughly 700,000 that Front Office Sports and Wikipedia give, so it is not a disagreement with them. Evidence: https://frontofficesports.com/terence-crawford-errol-spence-jr-bout-nets-around-700k-ppv-buys/, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Errol_Spence_Jr._vs._Terence_Crawford
- **derived**, 2026-10-03, claude-research: substack.com ppvRevenueUsd $55,000,000 (Terence Crawford vs Errol Spence Jr.). The $55 million is the 650,000 floor multiplied by the $84.99 price, which the page itself says ('generated a gross of more than $55 million'), not a figure anyone published separately; it moves with the buys figure it was computed from. Evidence: https://frontofficesports.com/terence-crawford-errol-spence-jr-bout-nets-around-700k-ppv-buys/
- **outlier**, 2026-10-03, claude-research: thesportster.com totalUsd $38,000,000 (Oleksandr Usyk vs Tyson Fury). The Sportster's own text says 'close to $38 million' and the page itself notes other outlets give $45 million; Wikipedia and MMA Mania, which are independent of each other, both give $45 million for Usyk's first-fight purse. Evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyson_Fury_vs._Oleksandr_Usyk, https://www.mmamania.com/2024/12/20/24326017/payouts-oleksandr-usyk-expected-to-bank-insane-105-million-for-tyson-fury-rematch-salaries-riyadh
- **outlier**, 2026-10-03, claude-research: foxnews.com ppvPriceUsd $50 (Oscar De La Hoya vs Floyd Mayweather Jr.). A 2013 passing comparison ('sold for $50') against HBO's own suggested retail price of $54.95 reported before the fight by Multichannel News, which Wikipedia rounds to $55. Fox's figure is a round number from memory of a six-year-old fight; the contemporaneous price is the better evidence. Evidence: https://www.nexttv.com/news/hbo-follow-de-la-hoyamayweather-247-331731, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_De_La_Hoya_vs._Floyd_Mayweather_Jr.
- **floor**, 2026-10-03, claude-research: nexttv.com ppvBuys 800,000 (Manny Pacquiao vs Ricky Hatton). 'Over the 800,000 mark' is a preliminary industry estimate, a lower bound given before HBO's numbers came in; ESPN's roughly 830,000 and Wikipedia's roughly 850,000 are consistent with it and with each other. Evidence: https://www.espn.com/sports/boxing/news/story?id=4674275, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manny_Pacquiao_vs._Ricky_Hatton
- **outlier**, 2026-10-03, claude-research: wbaboxing.com guaranteedUsd $13,000,000 (Sugar Ray Leonard vs Marvin Hagler). A 2023 retrospective gives Hagler a $13 million guarantee; Wikipedia and F4W Online (independent of each other) both say $12 million. Only the WBA piece, one source, says $13 million. Evidence: https://www.f4wonline.com/news/how-hagler-leonard-superfight-changed-combat-sports-landscape-233386/, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Hagler_vs._Sugar_Ray_Leonard, https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/boxing/30-years-later-richard-steele-recalls-epic-hagler-leonard-fight/
